questions.question: Locking your brakes can:

options.text: Help in most situations.
Make steering easier.
Cause you to lose control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause you to lose control.
questions.explanation: Locked brakes can cause you to lose control. If your front brake locks, release it and then apply it again. If your rear brake locks on a surface with good traction, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: It is illegal to ride a motorcycle with a blood alcohol level (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.08 percent or higher.
0.1 percent or higher.
0.3 percent or higher.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: In California, riders age 21 or older cannot legally ride with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Riders under 21 cannot ride with a BAC of 0.01 percent or higher. Even below the legal limit, alcohol can affect your riding ability.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster your body removes it.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: When you drink quickly, alcohol builds up in your body faster. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink in an hour, alcohol will still be in your system after an hour passes.

questions.question: When entering a turn, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Speed up.
Stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed before you enter a turn. Taking a turn too fast can cause you to drift out of your lane or off the road.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Ride carefully when approaching an intersection. Keep your hands ready on the clutch and both brakes so you can react quickly if needed.

questions.question: For motorcycle riders, a helmet is:

options.text: Not required if you have ridden for more than two years.
Recommended but not required.
Required.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required.
questions.explanation: In Virginia, motorcycle riders and passengers must wear helmets. A proper helmet is your best protection against head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders must wear:

options.text: A helmet.
A helmet if they choose to.
Nothing special.

questions.correctAnswerText: A helmet.
questions.explanation: In Georgia, you must wear a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards every time you ride a motorcycle.

questions.question: At night, when riding behind another vehicle, you can see bumps ahead by:

options.text: Listening to the other vehicle scrape the road.
Watching the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
Looking at the rear bumper to see if it bounces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watching the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
questions.explanation: Watch the vehicle ahead to judge road conditions at night. Its headlights show the road better than your high beam. If the taillights bounce up and down, there are bumps in the road ahead.

questions.question: Motorcycle mirrors:

options.text: Have blind spots, like car mirrors.
Have no blind spots.
Are not required.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots, like car mirrors.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots, just like car mirrors. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: At a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Position your motorcycle where other drivers can see you easily.
Stay close to the traffic control device.
Stay at the outside edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position your motorcycle where other drivers can see you easily.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to the part of your lane where other drivers will see you as soon as possible.

questions.question: To shift to a higher gear, you must:

options.text: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift it.
Place your foot over the shift lever and push it.
Use your thumb to move the lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift it.
questions.explanation: To shift to a higher gear, put your foot under the shift lever and lift it.

questions.question: You should use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch when:

options.text: The throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
You start to lose control in a curve.
The motorcycle starts to wobble.

questions.correctAnswerText: The throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
questions.explanation: If the throttle gets stuck and you cannot free it, turn off the engine and pull in the clutch right away. This removes power from the rear wheel so you can safely stop.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: Your mirrors show you everything around you.
Turn your head to check your blind spot, in addition to using mirrors.
Signal and move right or left immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot, in addition to using mirrors.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, even after checking your mirrors.

questions.question: Service signs are:

options.text: Orange with black letters.
Blue with white letters.
Green with white letters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: As your motorcycle goes faster, you will:

options.text: Need to shift up through the gears.
Need to shift down through the gears.
Need to put the motorcycle in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need to shift up through the gears.
questions.explanation: You must shift into higher gears as your motorcycle speeds up.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
Only stop if other traffic is coming.
Vehicles will enter the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians cross, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, the effects:

options.text: Are safer than using either one alone.
Cancel each other out.
Can be stronger than using either one alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be stronger than using either one alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can make riding unsafe. Some drugs become even more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends the SEE strategy for safe riding. What does "SEE" stand for?

options.text: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
Slow, Experienced, and Error-free.
Safe, Experienced, and Evasive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
questions.explanation: Good riders use the SEE strategy to make safe choices while riding. "SEE" means Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: The best way to stay safe while riding is to:

options.text: Look far ahead of your motorcycle.
Avoid areas with heavy traffic.
Ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: To avoid danger while riding, always watch the road far ahead. Look ahead to spot hazards before you reach them so you have time to react.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are separated by:

options.text: White lines.
Yellow lines.
Road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When should you inspect your motorcycle for safety?

options.text: Before every ride.
Every week.
Once a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Always inspect your motorcycle before you ride. Even small problems are more dangerous on a motorcycle than on a car.

questions.question: Your position in the lane should:

options.text: Help you blend in with traffic.
Give you a way to escape danger.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a way to escape danger.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see other drivers and lets them see you. It keeps you away from wind gusts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should stop other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Should you wear hearing protection when riding?

options.text: No, it is not recommended.
Yes, only for long rides.
Yes, for all rides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, for all rides.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a helmet on. Wear hearing protection every time you ride to protect your hearing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign appears on the back of vehicles moving slower than 25 mph, such as farm equipment, construction vehicles, or horse-drawn carts.

questions.question: When you approach a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic.
Skip the stop line and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop line and then go through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic.
questions.explanation: First, stop where the stop line or sign indicates. Then move forward slowly and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while you look.
